subject: Proposal: Service availability baseline & conditional credit schedule for CedarTech
messages:
From: Alex Gomez <agomez@cedartech.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@cedartech.com
Date: 2028-07-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: CedarTech SLA asks for evaluation

Soojin —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and platform engineering dug into the RFP and we have initial must-haves for the SLA. High-level:
- Availability: target 99.9% across hosted endpoints (global).
- Latency: p95 < 250ms for standard token lengths under our steady-state load.
- Monthly remediation/credit: mechanisms that are automatic and tied to measured availability and latency regressions.
- Exceptions: we want clear carveouts for scheduled maintenance, burst-provisioning, and any batched-inference maintenance windows.

I attached our SLA requirements document (CedarTech_RFP_SLA_Requirements.pdf) for reference.

Two asks from procurement: 1) a short proposal we can include in the SOW with explicit credit tiers and caps, 2) confirmation of whether you provide regional failover guarantees or only single-region commitments.

Could you send a short options memo by the end of next week? We have an internal review on the 19th.

—Alex
Alex Gomez
Director, Platform Engineering | CedarTech
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Alex Gomez <agomez@cedartech.com>
Cc: procurement@cedartech.com
Date: 2028-07-11T14:04:00Z
Subject: Re: CedarTech SLA asks for evaluation

Alex —

Appreciate the clear asks and the RFP. I've sketched two pragmatic options below so your team can weigh tradeoffs (availability vs. credit cap / exclusions). Short version up front: we recommend Option A (higher baseline with lower cap) for mission-critical production apps; Option B is available if you prefer a lower baseline with greater monetary protection.

Option A (Recommended) — Baseline-first
- Availability: 99.95% monthly for Hosted API.
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms measured from the primary region under steady-state traffic.
- Credits: tiered monthly service credits (applied as % of that month's invoice):
  * 99.95% — no credit
  * 99.50%–99.949% — 5% credit
  * 99.00%–99.499% — 10% credit
  * <99.00% — 15% credit (cap)
- Cap: maximum credit in any calendar month = 15% of the monthly invoice.
- Exceptions: scheduled maintenance with >=72 hours notice; capacity surge windows (documented in advance) and batched-inference maintenance windows.

Option B — Higher monetary protection
- Availability: 99.90% monthly.
- Credits: larger tiered credits: 10% / 15% / 25% with a monthly cap of 25% of the monthly invoice.
- Same exceptions as Option A plus a narrow carveout for capacity-constrained regional outages during major provider incidents.

Operational notes:
- Latency credits would only trigger if observed p95 latency regressions correlate with degraded availability or if the p95 exceeds the threshold for three consecutive measurement intervals in the month.
- We measure availability and latency using our observability pipeline (token-level success + p95 from the primary region). We can provide measurement reports for audit.

Next step: if either option looks reasonable we can run a short internal review with Legal/PS to tighten the maintenance carveouts and cap language. I can also surface a more polished appendix suitable for the SOW.

Attaching a working credit matrix spreadsheet for your procurement team to review.

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-12T08:22:00Z
Subject: FW: CedarTech SLA asks — options A/B (need legal + commercial redlines)

Marissa / Ben —

Forwarding CedarTech's RFP and my options draft. Summary: they asked for 99.9% and p95 250ms; I proposed Option A (99.95% / 15% cap) and Option B (99.9% / 25% cap).

Questions for quick input:
1) Commercial — is 15% monthly cap feasible for a mid-sized customer on a SaaS SOW? Any preference for cap expressed as dollars vs %?
2) Legal — maintenance carveouts: is 72 hrs reasonable? We should also add explicit language that credits are the exclusive remedy.
3) Measurement/audit — procurement will almost certainly want a measurement export for the 3-month lookback. Are we comfortable sharing token-level p95 export under NDA?

Requested turnaround: End of day 7/13. CedarTech has an internal review on 7/19.

Attachments: credit_matrix_v2.xlsx (working).

—Soojin
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-12T11:07:00Z
Subject: Re: FW: CedarTech SLA asks — options A/B (commercial feedback)

Soojin —

High-level commercial view: Option A looks fine as a recommended default. A few notes:
- Expressing caps as % of invoice is standard and easier for procurement; for high-volume customers we sometimes translate to a not-to-exceed dollar figure in the SOW.
- Recommend we tie the latency-triggered credits to customer-observed impact (e.g., error rates or sustained p95 breaches) to avoid noise-driven credits. Your wording on 3 consecutive measurement intervals is appropriate.
- Suggest an intermediate credit band between 99.00% and 99.50% (e.g., 7.5% instead of jumping 10%) to give finer gradation for small regressions. I've updated the attached credit matrix.

If Legal signs off on exclusive-remedy language and maintenance carveouts, we can send to CedarTech as an appendix.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Strategic Accounts
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-12T15:38:00Z
Subject: Re: FW: CedarTech SLA asks — legal redlines

Soojin / Marissa —

Quick legal redlines:
- Add: Scheduled maintenance with >=72 hours notice is excluded provided we publish a maintenance window on console and give an option to opt-out for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Add explicit exclusion for measures caused by customer-side misconfiguration or third-party dependencies we don't control.
- Add regional failover clause: we can commit to cross-region failover assistance but must include an operational runbook and a 30-day warm-up period for replication for private/dedicated deployments.
- Credits: confirm that credits are the exclusive remedy and they do not waive rights to equitable relief in case of gross negligence or willful misconduct.

I've attached a redlined PDF with the clause text (CedarTech_SLA_Redlines_20280712.pdf).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Alex Gomez <agomez@cedartech.com>, CedarTech Procurement <procurement@cedartech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-18T16:45:00Z
Subject: Final options: availability baseline, latency-triggered credits, and carveouts (two choices)

Alex / Team —

Thanks for the patience — below is a consolidated proposal reflecting commercial and legal input. I've tried to keep things simple so you can attach the preferred option to the SOW.

Option A (Recommended for production):
- Monthly availability: 99.95% (Hosted).
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms measured in the primary region. Latency credits apply only when p95 breaches correlate with increased error rates or with availability below 99.95% for three consecutive measurement intervals.
- Credit bands (% of monthly invoice): 0 / 5% / 7.5% / 15% (see attached credit_matrix_v2.xlsx).
- Monthly cap: 15% of the invoice.
- Exceptions: scheduled maintenance with >=72 hours notice (published on Console), customer misconfiguration, third-party provider outages, documented batched-inference maintenance windows. Regional failover assistance available per Appendix B (requires operational runbook).

Option B (Higher monetary protection):
- Monthly availability: 99.90%
- Latency: same measurement approach.
- Credit bands: 10% / 15% / 25% with monthly cap 25% of invoice.
- Additional carveout: excludes capacity-constrained provider-wide incidents where failover is infeasible.

Legal: credits are the exclusive monetary remedy except for gross negligence or willful misconduct. We will provide measurement exports for audit under NDA and can include a one-time three-month lookback on request.

Attachments: credit_matrix_v2.xlsx, CedarTech_SLA_Redlines_20280712.pdf.

Action requested: Please let me know which option you prefer (A or B) and whether you want us to pull together Appendix B as a signed DocuSign packet. If Option A is acceptable, we'll prepare the SOW appendix and a DocuSign link for signature by 7/21 so you can meet your internal 7/19 review (we can also provide a draft earlier if you need it).

Thanks —
